newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade down before US data.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade down before US data.

text.p: German blue chip shares ended bourse trade lower on Friday, undermined by the sharp overnight fall on Wall Street and on continued uncertainty ahead of the U.S. jobs data due later in the day.
The DAX index of Germany's 30 leading shares closed 12.54 points, or 0.50 percent, lower at 2,517 points amid very small trading volumes.
"People were surprised by the strength of the correction on Wall Street," one dealer said, referring to the 0.88 percent fall in the Dow Jones Industrial index overnight.
The stability of the dollar against the mark, largely unchanged at 1.4850/55 to the German currency, provided some support for share prices but no new gains until the U.S. data was out of the way.
"Trading will be limited until the impact of the figures on the dollar is seen," one deale said.
Concern centred around the possibility that a strong gain in U.S. payrolls could provide the key for a near-term raise in U.S. interest rates, which would make German stock yirleds less attractive.

With the consensus forecast that the U.S. payroll figure for August would be some 244,000 than the montH before, dealers said any increase of 250,000-plus would be enough to generate fears of a rate hike.

Individual stock activity was limited. Shares in Germany's largest commercial bank, Deutsche Bank AG, closed 85 pfennigs lower at 71.50 after a newspaper report cited an admission by the bank of control failures at its British asset management arm Morgan Grenfell.
